oneLine: Owns door time: who may use which dock door and when. It books, moves and cancels appointments, and follows the truck's real arrival and door from the yard.

rows.title: Book a time window at a dock door
rows.story: A carrier books a window at a door. It is refused if the door is closed or out of hours, the ASNs are unknown or already booked, the carrier is suspended, or another booking overlaps.

then.does: keeps a copy of the booking so the gate can match the arriving truck
adds the booking to its view of expected inbound demand
keeps a copy of inbound bookings
for an outbound booking with a cut-off, assigns the door to that load

rows.title: Move a booking to another window or door
rows.story: A carrier moves a booked appointment to a new window, or to another door. The same checks as a new booking apply. The event keeps the previous window and door.

then.does: updates its copy; frees held yard moves if the door changed
moves the booking in its expected inbound demand
updates the window and door in its copy

rows.title: Cancel a booking
rows.story: The carrier or the dock planner cancels a booked or checked-in appointment with a reason. The door window is freed.

then.does: marks it cancelled in its copy and frees held yard moves
records the cancellation in its expected inbound demand
marks it cancelled in its copy

rows.title: Report that a truck will be late
rows.story: A carrier reports when the truck will arrive. If that is later than the window plus the site's tolerance, the booking is flagged at risk. An ETA inside the tolerance clears an earlier flag.

rows.title: Cancel when every ASN of a booking is cancelled
rows.story: inbound-receiving announces that an ASN was cancelled. The ASN is marked cancelled in the local copy, and a booked inbound appointment whose ASNs are all cancelled is cancelled too.
rows.policy: Whenever the last ASN of a booked inbound appointment is cancelled, cancel the appointment

then.does: marks it cancelled in its copy and frees held yard moves
records the cancellation in its expected inbound demand
marks it cancelled in its copy

rows.title: Cancel when the gate turns a truck away
rows.story: The yard refuses a visit at the gate. If its appointment is still booked, it is cancelled with the reason 'turned away'. Any other state is ignored and counted.
rows.policy: Whenever the gate turns a visit away, cancel its booked appointment

then.does: marks it cancelled in its copy and frees held yard moves
records the cancellation in its expected inbound demand
marks it cancelled in its copy

rows.title: Note that the truck is at the gate
rows.story: The yard checks a truck in against a booking. The appointment becomes checked in and records whether the truck was early, on time or late.
rows.policy: Whenever a visit checks in against a booked appointment, record the arrival as early, on time or late

rows.title: Follow the truck to the door it really used
rows.story: If a trailer docks at a different door than the booked one, the real door wins and the booking moves there, even over another booking. Bookings it now overlaps are flagged at risk.
rows.policy: Whenever a trailer docks at another door than booked, the actual door wins

then.does: updates the appointment's door in its copy, so a receipt records the right door

rows.title: Close the booking when the trailer leaves the door
rows.story: When the yard reports the trailer undocked, the appointment is completed. If this news arrives before the gate check-in, the arrival is recorded as implicit.
rows.policy: Whenever a trailer leaves its door, complete the appointment it came for

rows.title: Sweep for carriers that never came
rows.story: A scheduler calls the sweep. Every booked appointment whose window plus the site's grace period has passed becomes a no-show. A no-show is final: a late carrier has to book again.
rows.policy: Every sweep, mark each booked appointment whose window and grace have passed as a no-show

then.does: marks it a no-show in its copy and frees held yard moves
records the no-show in its expected inbound demand
opens an exception case for the no-show, or updates the open one

rows.title: Declare when a site's doors operate
rows.story: A dock planner sets the operating hours of a site's doors. New hours that would strand an active appointment are refused.

rows.title: Close a door for a while
rows.story: A dock planner closes a door for a period, for example for repairs. It is refused if it overlaps another closure or covers an active appointment.

then.does: keeps the closure in its copy

rows.title: Reopen a closed door
rows.story: A dock planner lifts a scheduled closure early, and the door can be booked again.

then.does: removes the closure from its copy

rows.title: Add a carrier to the registry
rows.story: A planner records a carrier under its SCAC code. The registry is optional: a carrier that is not in it can still book. Changing its details later raises the same event again.

then.does: keeps a copy of the carrier registry

rows.title: Suspend a carrier
rows.story: A planner suspends a carrier. Bookings and moves that name it are refused until it is reinstated. Appointments it already has stay as they are.

then.does: keeps the carrier's suspended status in its copy

rows.title: Reinstate a suspended carrier
rows.story: A planner lets a suspended carrier book again.

then.does: keeps the carrier's active status in its copy

hotspots.text: Pickups from cut-offs are not built. The cut-off schedule is stored, but no outbound appointment is created, and the door rule and lead time are undefined.
A retired door blocks new bookings only. Appointments already on it are left untouched.
Appointment facts do not yet say whether an agent made the change. Only carrier facts carry that attribution so far.
The carrier registry is opt-in: a carrier that was never registered can still book. Only a suspended one is refused.

opportunities.text: A strict mode, where a named carrier must be registered to book, is a future per-site setting. It needs the registry populated first.
A carrier-connectivity context could translate these facts into partner formats. The ADR leaves that decision pending with the owner.
